data.title: BlackSun Raises $1 Billion for Sports and Media Fund
data.description:
BlackSun raised $1 billion for a new sports and media fund, according to Bloomberg.

BlackSun CEO Antonn Muhammed said the private equity firm believes in "compassionate capitalism" and aims to provide services for everyone as well as investors. Former boxing world champion Roy Jones Jr., who leads BlackSun's boxing group Knockout Fights, said the new venture includes physical and financial protections for athletes in a dangerous sport.

data.title: Morgan Stanley Highlights Dividend Stocks as September Trading Turns Volatile
data.description: According to CNBC, Morgan Stanley screened the Russell 1000 for companies that raised dividends by at least 15% quarter over quarter in the past 12 months and highlighted East West Bancorp, Packaging Corporation of America and Devon Energy among its picks. East West Bancorp raised its quarterly dividend by 20 cents to 80 cents a share in January, reported second-quarter earnings of $2.63 per share on revenue of $791 million in July, and lifted its full-year net interest income growth forecast to 7% to 9% from 6% to 8%. Packaging Corporation of America increased its quarterly dividend by 20% in May, bringing the annual payout to $6 a share. Devon Energy, which Morgan Stanley called its favorite exploration and production name in the sector on Friday as oil prices approached $100 a barrel, raised its dividend to 32 cents per share in May. Morgan Stanley strategist Todd Castagno said dividends can provide a steady income stream, signal confidence to the market and help stabilize portfolios during periods of uncertainty and high valuations.

data.title: US President Donald Trump Says Higher Rates Will Not Calm Bond Market
data.description: US President Donald Trump said raising interest rates would not calm the bond market and reiterated that he wants rates to fall. According to Sina Finance, he made the remarks at the White House while taking questions from reporters about bonds. Trump also said U.S. interest rates should be 1% or 0.5%, and repeated that the United States should have the lowest interest rates in the world.

data.title: Bessent Sees Oil Falling to $40 After Iran Conflict Ends
data.description:

data.title: AI | Anthropic Expands Credit Facility to $15 Billion Before IPO Filing
data.description:
Anthropic is finalizing an expansion of its revolving credit facility to $15 billion before its anticipated public filing, according to Bloomberg.

Bloomberg also reported that the US jobs report showed the IT sector shed 23,000 jobs in August, while Apple is starting the John Ternus era with what could be the biggest run of new devices in its history.

data.title: How Americans Are Coping With Rising College Costs
data.description:
The average cost of a four-year degree is about $60,000 at private colleges and $26,000 at public universities, while student loan defaults topped 9 million in June, according to Bloomberg.

Bloomberg's Scarlet Fu visited SUNY Purchase in Westchester County, New York, to speak with students, parents and the university president about how they are thinking about money.

data.title: Anthropic's $15 Billion Credit Line Prepares It for IPO
data.description:
Anthropic's planned $15 billion revolving credit facility is strengthening its position ahead of a potential IPO, according to Bloomberg.

Rainmaker Securities co-founder and Managing Director Greg Martin said Anthropic's rapid growth could support a valuation above SpaceX's at IPO and that a successful debut could open the door for other long-awaited tech listings, including Oura and neoclouds.

data.title: AI Shrinks Entry-Level Tech Hiring as US Information Jobs Fall 23,000
data.description:
The US information sector shed roughly 23,000 jobs in August, according to Bloomberg, as AI continues to reshape the labor market.

Northeastern University Professor Alicia Modestino said tech may be the “canary in the coal mine,” citing research that shows a decline in junior versus senior software developer vacancies since ChatGPT’s release. She said employers are demanding more experience, judgment and human-centric skills from entry-level workers.
